Leonida
  

Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

  Other languages |

  Want to help? |
  Credits |

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded
and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs
are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this
happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You
> need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection.
> Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes
> from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files.

Discord: https://discord.gg/rexed

Custom Git Mirror: https://git.notrexed.dev/notrexed/Leonida

oss.description: Chrome Extension (MV3) to switch Google's mandatory QR code verification back to standard 6-digit SMS verification via iPad Mini profile & [3,null,4] RPC fallback.
oss.readme:
# Google QR SMS Helper (`google-qr-sms-helper`)

  
  
  
  

  将 Google 桌面端强制跨设备扫码验证（MO-SMS / GMS Constellation）一键降级回传统的「输入手机号接收 6 位短信验证码」流程。
  Switch Google's mandatory cross-device QR verification back to standard 6-digit SMS / Voice verification on desktop browsers.

---

## 📦 一、安装教程 (Installation)

### 方式 1：直接下载 Release 压缩包（推荐新手）
1. 前往本仓库的 **[Releases 页面](https://github.com/havenicec/google-qr-sms-helper/releases/latest)**，下载最新的 `google-qr-sms-helper-v1.1.0.zip` 并解压到本地文件夹。
2. 打开 Chrome / Edge / Brave 浏览器，在地址栏输入 `chrome://extensions/` 并回车。
3. 打开页面右上角的 **「开发者模式 (Developer mode)」** 开关。
4. 点击左上角的 **「加载已解压的扩展程序 (Load unpacked)」**，选中刚才解压出来的文件夹即可完成安装。

### 方式 2：通过 Git 克隆安装
```bash
git clone https://github.com/havenicec/google-qr-sms-helper.git
```
然后在 `chrome://extensions/` 中开启「开发者模式」，点击「加载已解压的扩展程序」并选择 `google-qr-sms-helper` 目录。

---

## 🚀 二、保姆级图文使用教程 (Step-by-Step Usage Guide)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **核心前提（必看）**：**不要**直接从第三方客户端（如 Antigravity / Gemini Code Assist 授权页）弹出的二维码页面降级（因为其 `continue` 参数包含多层嵌套重定向，会被 Google 重新拦截回二维码）。  
> **必须先打开 Google Cloud Console 通过 Cloud Shell 唤出原生的 `Verify` 窗口**！在这里过完一次短信验证后，你的 Google 账号权限将全局解锁，再回 Antigravity 等工具登录即可直接丝滑通过。

### 第 1 步：打开 Google Cloud Console 并唤起 Cloud Shell 验证
1. 在浏览器中登录你需要验证的 Google 账号，访问 **[https://console.cloud.google.com/](https://console.cloud.google.com/)**。
2. 如下图所示，点击页面右上角导航栏的 **「激活 Cloud Shell」终端图标 `[>_]`**（或者直接点击页面右下角插件悬浮窗里的 **`1. 自动点击 Cloud Shell 终端图标`** 按钮）。
3. 在底部弹出的 `Verify your account` 窗口中，点击蓝色的 **`Verify`** 按钮：

![Cloud Shell Verify 入口示意](./assets/cloud-shell-verify.png)

---

### 第 2 步：在二维码页面点击「一键降级到短信选择框」
1. 点击 `Verify` 后，会弹出 Google 的二维码验证页面（`/v3/signin/challenge/iap/qrcode`）。
2. 等待二维码图片加载出来后，点击页面右下角插件悬浮面板上的 **「⚡ 一键降级到短信选择框」** 按钮：
   - 插件会自动调用浏览器原生 `BarcodeDetector` 识别页面上的二维码；
   - 自动在后台向 Google 发送 `MypxBd` 与 `YDtwf ([null, uuid, dsh, 7, null, tl, false])` 数据包，拿到 `[3, null, 4]`（非 Android 设备回退短信验证状态）；
   - 自动将当前标签页的请求头与环境伪装为 **`iPad Mini`**（无需手动按 F12 切换设备），并重定向到 `uplevelingstep/selection?...&idv_xdevice=1`。

---

### 第 3 步：选择「短信 (Text message)」并输入手机号接码
1. 页面会自动跳转进带有单选框的 **验证方式选择页 (`/uplevelingstep/selection`)**：
   - 勾选 **Text message (SMS) / 短信**（或语音通话），点击下一步。
2. 在手机号输入框中填入你的接码手机号（支持任意国家/地区的接码平台号码或实体卡号），点击发送验证码。
3. 收到 `G-xxxxxx` 的 6 位数字验证码后填入并点击 **Next**，即可完成账号验证！
4. 验证通过后，回到 Cloud Shell 或 Antigravity / Gemini CLI 刷新即可正常使用。

---

## ❓ 三、常见问题与避坑指南 (FAQ & Troubleshooting)

### Q1: 为什么我从别的链接点进二维码页，点降级后又跳回了二维码？
- **原因**：只有从 `https://console.cloud.google.com/` 点击右上角 **Cloud Shell `[>_]` -> `Verify`** 唤出的二维码页，其 `continue` 参数才是纯净的 `https://accounts.google.com/uplevelingstep/selection?TL=...&authuser=0&flowName=GlifWebSignIn&sarp=1&scc=1`。请务必按「第 1 步」从 Cloud Shell 入口进入。

### Q2: 为什么插件默认伪装成 `iPad Mini` 而不是 `iPad Pro` 或桌面浏览器？
- **原因**：Google 的 `uplevelingstep/selection` 接口会校验 `User-Agent`：
  - 桌面端（Windows / macOS）以及 Chrome F12 中的 `iPad Pro 13` 发送的都是 `Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X` 桌面级 UA，Google 检测到桌面环境会无视 `idv_xdevice=1` 强行跳回二维码。
  - 而 `iPad Mini` 发送的是纯移动端 `iPad; CPU OS 16_6 like Mac OS X ... Mobile/15E148` 请求头，且在提交 6 位验证码的 `/_/IdvUplevelingUi/data/batchexecute` 接口上必须保持前后完全一致的 `iPad Mini` 请求头（已在 v1.1.0 中通过 `declarativeNetRequest` 全路径自动覆盖，无需手动开 F12）。

### Q3: 点击「一键降级」提示“未能在当前页面识别到二维码”怎么办？
- 请确认使用的是 **Chrome / Edge 88+** 浏览器（支持原生 `BarcodeDetector` 接口），并等待页面上的黑色二维码图案完全显示后再点击按钮。

---

## ✨ 四、技术原理与工作流 (Architecture & Workflow)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Desktop Browser (User)
    participant E as Extension (Content + DNR)
    participant B as Background Service Worker
    participant G as Google Identity Backend

    U->>G: 1. Trigger Verify from Cloud Console (Cloud Shell)
    G-->>U: Render /v3/signin/challenge/iap/qrcode
    U->>E: 2. Click "⚡ 一键降级到短信选择框"
    E->>E: Decode QR Canvas/Image via native BarcodeDetector
    E->>B: Send QR URL (devicephoneverification/begin)
    B->>G: POST MypxBd (SelectNextVerificationMethod -> consent)
    B->>G: GET /devicephoneverification/consent (extract request UUID)
    B->>G: POST YDtwf [null, uuid, dsh, 7, null, tl, false]
    G-->>B: Return ["wrb.fr", "YDtwf", "[3, null, 4]"] (Non-Android Fallback)
    B-->>E: Fallback state locked
    E->>G: Redirect to uplevelingstep/selection?...&idv_xdevice=1 (with iPad Mini UA)
    G-->>U: Render SMS / Voice Radio Selection & 6-Digit Code Input
```

---

## 📁 目录结构 (Project Structure)

```text
google-qr-sms-helper/
├── assets/
│   └── cloud-shell-verify.png  # Cloud Shell Verify 入口示意图
├── manifest.json               # Chrome Extension Manifest V3 配置文件
├── background.js               # DNR 全路径 iPad Mini 请求头伪装 + [3,null,4] RPC 注入
├── content.js                  # 悬浮控制面板 + BarcodeDetector 二维码识别 + URL 清洗跳转
├── ua_spoof.js                 # Main-world navigator 属性对齐
├── LICENSE                     # MIT 开源协议
└── README.md                   # 项目说明与图文教程
```

---

oss.readme:
Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow.

  

  
  
  
  
  
  
  

Rewriting a whole app in Rust costs months, minute-long compiles and gigabytes of `target/`. Most of the runtime sits in a few functions anyway.

**fast-anything** finds those functions, has your coding agent port *only them* to Rust, proves the port gives the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. One command, fully reversible.

## Install

```sh
npm i -g @el4cteo/fast-anything      # or: cargo install fast-anything
```

Ports are compiled with your Rust toolchain ([rustup](https://rustup.rs)).

## Use

```sh
fast-anything go --agent claude -- python app.py     # or: -- node app.ts / bun app.ts / deno run -A app.ts / ruby app.rb / java App.java / mvn exec:java / gradle run / go run . / php app.php / clang -O2 main.c / Rscript app.R
```

Or step by step:

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `scan -- ` | profiles the app, ranks functions by time × how portable they are |
| `port [id]` | records up to 500 real calls, creates a one-function Rust crate + `TASK.md` |
| `verify` | release-builds the port and replays every recorded call |
| `enable` / `disable` | swaps the Rust in or out (one marked block, removed byte for byte) |
| `bench` | times the whole app, original vs Rust, interleaved runs |
| `report` | markdown + SVG card for your PR |
| `doctor` | checks Rust, your runtimes and your agents |

`--agent` takes `claude`, `codex`, or any command that reads a prompt on stdin. Without it, hand `TASK.md` to whatever you use.

## Proof, not vibes

That port looked right but compared bytes instead of characters. 148 of 500 real calls caught it. On top of the recorded calls, fast-anything derives extra cases and lets the original answer them: edge cases (NaN, ±infinity, -0.0, zero and ±1, non-ASCII text, empty and up to 16× bigger inputs) and shrunk inputs (tiny and random slices). Nothing is enabled until every case matches: same values (floats within 1e-9), errors where the original errors. A port that is right but slower per call than the original (calling into Rust costs more than the work saved) isn't enabled either. `FAST_ANYTHING_DISABLE=1` runs the original any time.

## Results

Real runs on an i5-10500, Windows 11 (C and C++: a 4-core GitHub Actions Linux runner). Reproduce them from [`examples/`](examples).

| app | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Python fuzzy dedupe (700 names) | 4.91s | **42ms, 116×** |
| TypeScript fuzzy dedupe (2,000 names) | 3.11s | **155ms, 20×** |
| PHP fuzzy dedupe (600 names) | 2.94s | **53ms, 55×** |
| Go fuzzy dedupe (3,000 names) | 3.02s | **144ms, 21×** |
| Ruby fuzzy dedupe (400 names) | 3.13s | **228ms, 14×** |
| C# fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 4.03s | **312ms, 13×** |
| Java fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 3.50s | **1.18s, 3×** (11× on the function; the rest is JVM startup) |
| C mandelbrot (8 zoom levels) | 431ms | **127ms, 3.4×** |
| C++ fuzzy dedupe (6,000 names) | 3.02s | **1.09s, 2.7×** |

fast-anything ports the outermost loop it can, not the tiny function called inside it, so the app crosses into Rust once instead of millions of times. Porting only the inner `levenshtein` gave 35× and 1.9×.

## Why not rewrite it all?

- **Compile time**: each port is a one-function crate. Seconds, not minutes.
- **Cache**: every port shares one `.fast/target`. Delete it whenever you like.
- **Risk**: your code stays as it is. Rust is opt-in per function, checked against real behavior.

## Agents

- **Claude Code plugin**: `/plugin marketplace add EL4CTEO/fast-anything`, then `/plugin install fast-anything@fast-anything` and `/fast-anything:fast python app.py`
- **MCP server** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…), built into the binary: `claude mcp add fast-anything -- fast-anything mcp`. 8 tools: `fast_scan`, `fast_port`, `fast_verify`, `fast_enable`, `fast_disable`, `fast_bench`, `fast_report`, `fast_status`.
- **Skill**: [`skills/fast-anything`](skills/fast-anything/SKILL.md) teaches any agent the loop.

## Languages

| language | binding | status |
|---|---|---|
| Python 3.10+ | PyO3 | ✅ |
| JavaScript / TypeScript (Node 22+, Bun, Deno 2+: `bun app.ts`, `deno run -A app.ts`) | napi-rs | ✅ |
| Ruby 3.3+ | C ABI + JSON, through Ruby's built-in Fiddle | ✅ |
| Java 22+ (`java App.java`, Maven, Gradle) | the same C bridge, through the FFM API | ✅ |
| Kotlin/JVM (Gradle, `src/main/kotlin`, JDK 22+) | the Java bridge; top-level functions, `object` and companion members, extension functions | ✅ |
| Go 1.22+ (`go run .`) | the same C bridge, through the Windows loader or dlopen (cgo) | ✅ |
| PHP 8.1+ (`php app.php`) | the same C bridge, through PHP's FFI extension (`extension=ffi`) | ✅ |
| C and C++ (gcc, clang or Intel oneAPI icx/icpx: `clang -O2 main.c lib.c`) | the same C bridge, through LoadLibrary or dlopen | ✅ |
| C# / .NET 8+ (`dotnet run -c Release`) | the same C bridge, through NativeLibrary; profiled with EventPipe, nothing to install | ✅ |
| R 4.0+ (`Rscript app.R`) | the same C bridge, through base R's `.C()`; profiled with Rprof, no packages or R headers needed | ✅ |

It ports top-level, deterministic functions that take plain data (numbers, strings, lists, dicts, typed arrays…), including ones in your entry script when its main code sits under `if __name__ == "__main__":` (or `if __FILE__ == $0`, or `if (import.meta.main)` / `if (require.main === module)`). In Python that means module-level functions and `@staticmethod`s (dataclasses, NamedTuples and numeric NumPy arrays count as plain data), in Java, C# and PHP static methods (and PHP functions), in Go plain functions, in C and C++ free functions and static methods. `scan` says why anything else can't move yet.

With Intel oneAPI on Windows, run fast-anything from a shell where `setvars.bat` ran (it sets up the linker). SYCL kernels run on the device and aren't ported; with `-fsycl`, only host functions are profiled and ported.

rust-anything

Rewrite your app in Rust, and prove it still behaves the same.
Point it at your app: it records what the original does, your coding agent writes the Rust one piece at a time,
and every piece is checked against that recording before it moves on. It doesn't translate code; it proves the rewrite.

  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  

Install · Releases · Claude Code plugin · MCP Registry · Real-world ports · FAQ
Languages · How it works · Whole apps · Sponsors · MIT
Made in Türkiye 🇹🇷 by erKam Yaman · ❤️ Sponsor me · Sponsored by  CodeRabbit

Also by me: safe-anything, a 100% Rust security scanner for code, secrets, configs and AI agent setups. Find the holes before someone else does.

New in 2.0: Prettier, ported to Rust. 19x faster · 15,861 of 17,224 recorded runs fully in Rust · every run byte-identical

  
  
  Prettier against its Rust port on 59 real files from ms, Fuse.js and json-server (Apple M4). Same output, byte for byte. How it was measured.

PHP and C#: unit ports, through FFI and P/Invoke.

  
    
      Record
      record runs the original on generated edge cases, semantic traps and your own inputs, and saves what it returns or throws.
    
    
      Port
      bridge generates the Rust crate and a wrapper, so callers keep the original API. You or your agent write the Rust.
    
    
      Check
      diff replays every recorded case against the Rust, and nothing ships until they all match and gate passes.
    
    
      Lift
      When replay passes with no fallback and every unit passes gate, app lift makes it a pure Rust app. The original is never touched.
    
  

**Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time.** rust-anything records what your
Node.js (TypeScript/JavaScript), Python, C, Go, Ruby, Java or Kotlin app does today, then checks every piece of the
Rust rewrite against that recording before it moves on, until the app is pure Rust. CLIs, HTTP
servers and libraries; your coding agent (or you) writes the Rust. It is built on
[napi-rs](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs), [PyO3](https://github.com/PyO3/pyo3) and
[wasm-bindgen](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen), which carry the calls between your
language and Rust; rust-anything decides what to move and proves it matches. It can only catch what the
recording covers: see [What it can't catch](docs/how-it-works.md#what-it-cant-catch). Whole tools
and servers, or only the slow part, one hot path at a time:

| Real project, same output as the original | Original | With rust-anything |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| [Prettier](docs/real-world.md#prettier) 3.6.2, 2,360 JS/TS files from the command line | 128.6 s | **6.9 s: 19x faster** |
| Prettier, 6,305 Markdown files from the command line | 352 s | **22.5 s: 15.6x faster** |
| [json-server](docs/real-world.md#json-server), a whole Node server: memory at idle | 74 MB | **3.5 MB**, one 5.3 MB binary |
| json-server, from start to first response | 79 to 85 ms | **8 to 10 ms** |
| [Fuse.js](docs/real-world.md#fusejs) search over 50,000 strings, per query | 91.2 ms | **2.8 ms: 32x faster** |

Prettier: 15,861 of 17,224 recorded runs format fully in Rust across 10 languages (JavaScript,
TypeScript, JSX, JSON, GraphQL, YAML, Markdown, CSS, SCSS, Less), and all 17,224 match Prettier
byte for byte, since anything not ported yet falls back to Prettier. json-server: 514/514
recorded HTTP cases match on a pure Rust binary. Measured on an Apple M4, two runs each, every
output compared before timing ([details](docs/real-world.md)). Calling Rust once per small
function is usually *slower* than a JIT; rust-anything finds the loop worth moving, and moves it. Against
C the win is safety, not speed: [ffmpeg's libavutil](docs/real-world.md#ffmpeg) ported to Rust
matches all 226,447 recorded calls and runs at about C's speed (18 of 42 benchmarks even, 8
faster, 16 slower by 3 to 40%).

## Only the slow part

You don't have to port the whole app. Point `go` at a command that is too slow, and it ports
the one function that takes the time:

```sh
rust-anything go --agent claude -- python3 app.py
```

It profiles the run, picks the outermost function worth moving (the loop, not the small call
inside it, batched where the profile says so), records it on generated inputs plus the calls your
run makes, and hands `src/port.rs` to your agent (`claude`, `codex`, or any command that reads a
prompt on stdin; without `--agent` it writes `TASK.md` for you and stops). It switches the
function on only when every recorded case matches and `gate` passes. Then:

```sh
rust-anything report rust/dedupe-rs     # REPORT.md and card.svg for the pull request
rust-anything disable rust/dedupe-rs    # back to the original, byte for byte
```

The [Fuse.js](docs/real-world.md#fusejs) row above is this shape: Fuse's score for one string,
batched over the list, moved to Rust while object keys, extended search and the rest stay in
JavaScript, for 91.2 ms to 2.8 ms per query over 50,000 strings. Try `go` on
[`tests/fixtures/go-fuzzy`](tests/fixtures/go-fuzzy), a 20-line Python dedupe. Every way to switch
a port on and off: [Switch a port on and off](docs/how-it-works.md#switch-a-port-on-and-off).

  
  
  json-server, a whole Node server, lifted to a pure Rust binary (Apple M4). How it was measured.

> `record` and `app record` run your original code, calling each function (or the whole app) on
> many generated inputs, and `app record` runs every case twice. `diff`, `gate` and `app replay`
> run the same cases again, on the port or the original. Code that writes files, talks to a

### Minor Changes

- [#17060](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/17060) [`fa50aba`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/fa50abac64e5d9a3e5daa7258c8cf816a90c5349) Thanks [@petebacondarwin](https://github.com/petebacondarwin)! - Support `--env-file` in the experimental `cf-wrangler dev` delegate

  Wrangler-bundled projects can now use `cf dev -- --env-file ../../.env` to load a shared development file outside the project directory without enabling `CLOUDFLARE_INCLUDE_PROCESS_ENV`. Repeat `--env-file` to load multiple files, with later files overriding earlier values.

- [#17093](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/17093) [`310633d`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/310633d2c435d7035f706fbf08052b8d9d910857) Thanks [@for-the-kidz](https://github.com/for-the-kidz)! - Remove the `wrangler dispatch-namespace rename` command

  Renaming a Workers for Platforms dispatch namespace left the namespace name stored in dispatcher bindings out of date, which could make Workers in the namespace impossible to read or delete by name. The Cloudflare API now rejects requests that change a dispatch namespace's name, so the command has been removed. To use a different name, create a new dispatch namespace and redeploy your Workers to it.
